title: AEGIS: Preventing Cross-Domain Resource Abuse in MCP
V93_REASON: AEGIS is a runtime policy-enforcement component for MCP tool invocations. It normalizes heterogeneous live requests into a policy-friendly representation and integrates with Open Policy Agent/ContextForge to detect and mitigate resource-abusive invocations before backend effects, constituting an explicit governed invocation-to-effect boundary.
V93_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: IBM Research DSN 2026 publication page + DSN 2026 accepted-paper record

title: MCP-Scanner: Detecting Security Risks in Model Context Protocol Systems
V93_REASON: MCP-Scanner automatically audits MCP servers for vulnerabilities before exposure to production agents. This is preventive ecosystem/server security assessment rather than runtime revalidation of a pending consequential action.
V93_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Cyber Science Lab publication page; EnCyCriS 2026

title: MPMA: Preference Manipulation Attack Against Model Context Protocol
V93_REASON: MPMA introduces and experimentally validates preference-manipulation attacks that bias MCP tool/server selection. It exposes a decision-selection vulnerability and calls for defenses, but does not itself implement a mechanism preserving/revalidating consequential execution validity.

title: MSA: A Cross-MCP Privacy Attack via Memory Exfiltration of Large Language Models
V93_REASON: MSA implements and validates a malicious MCP-server memory-exfiltration attack in commercial MCP hosts. It demonstrates unauthorized data effects but contributes an attack, not a runtime protection/revalidation mechanism.

title: Bridging AI and software security: A comparative vulnerability assessment of LLM agent deployment paradigms
V93_REASON: Large empirical vulnerability assessment compares Function Calling and MCP across 3,250 attack scenarios. It provides threat evidence and secure-deployment guidance but does not implement an execution-time validity/authority gate.

title: A Comprehensive Security Framework for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Multi-Agent AI Systems
V93_REASON: Paper proposes an MCP Server Standard Framework with authentication/authorization, supply-chain defense, observability and secure-by-design controls for sensitive multi-agent applications. It directly addresses execution governance, but accessible evidence establishes a proposed security framework rather than a clearly validated per-action governed commit mechanism.

title: Behavioural analysis of independent value-based learning in non-cooperative games
V93_REASON: Study is conventional independent value-based multi-agent reinforcement learning in non-cooperative games, evaluated in a Food Chain simulation and focused on Nash-equilibrium convergence. It is outside the contemporary LLM/agentic tool-execution decision-validity mechanism scope.
V93_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Taylor & Francis article + UWE institutional repository full text

title: Embodied Intelligence: Smooth Coping in the Learning Intelligent Decision Agent Cognitive Architecture
V93_REASON: 2022 hypothesis/theory article develops a conceptual smooth-coping model in the LIDA cognitive architecture. It predates the target contemporary LLM/agentic tool-execution paradigm and does not study a validity-preserving consequential commit boundary.
V93_EVIDENCE_SOURCE: Frontiers in Psychology full text / PMC
